page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-8 is a compute-oriented instance within the network-optimized tier, powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C x86_64 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The instance provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 16 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache architecture features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. The CPU incorporates modern hardware acceleration extensions, including AVX-512 (Foundation, VNNI, BF16), AMX matrix acceleration (Tile, INT8), and cryptographic primitives such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance does not include local storage or bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on network-attached volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark assessments reveal top-tier single-threaded capability alongside competitive integer performance. Single-core Geekbench results reach the top 10 percent bracket, supported by strong single-threaded text processing and compression metrics in gzip and bzip3 testing. The integrated AMX instructions enable efficient lightweight model execution, evidenced by top-tier text generation speeds for small 135M language models. Conversely, multi-core throughput in stress-ng and Geekbench scales within the median range due to the 4-core physical count. Memory-intensive operations reflect typical DDR throughput, recording 61.58 GB/s in large uncached reads and 35.51 GB/s in large writes. Furthermore, medium-sized language model generation exhibits reduced throughput, constrained by the 16 GB memory ceiling.

From an infrastructure perspective, the c4n-highcpu-8 instance delivers compute efficiency for tasks requiring modern instruction sets without paying for unneeded memory capacity. The absence of integrated NVMe drives means all storage I/O must traverse virtual network disks, which organizations should factor into latency-sensitive storage designs. The platform is strategically suited for text processing pipelines, data compression tasks, compilation and CI/CD pipelines, containerized application runtimes, and algorithmic services that benefit directly from dedicated Intel Xeon vector instructions.

The instance offers a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU and includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions.
